matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the numeric difference between the two sides. This establishes how much the left or right side must change to achieve equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Treating 'XV = VIII + II' as 15 = 10 without computing the 5‑unit discrepancy leads to random stick moves.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be removed from a character and added to another, ensuring both source and destination remain valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When generating candidate moves after the numeric discrepancy is known.
matchstick.example: Assuming a stick can be taken from 'X' and left as a valid numeral, which is false because a single diagonal is not a Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, calculate how the numeric values of the affected numerals change and check whether the net change equals the previously computed discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After enumerating candidate moves, to filter those that could balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick that changes 'V' (5) to 'X' (10) adds 5, matching a discrepancy of 5; ignoring this leads to moves that cannot balance the equation.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into '-', and removing the horizontal stick turns it into 'I'. Use this when a stick must be taken from or added to a plus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a candidate move involves the plus operator as source or destination.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' and forgetting that the operator becomes '-', then failing to account for the sign change.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick to a numeral changes its value by the needed amount, consider moving a stick from an operator (e.g., '+' or '-') to that numeral, while ensuring the operator remains a valid symbol after removal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When no direct numeral‑to‑numeral transformation matches the discrepancy, but an operator can supply a stick.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to an 'I' to create a 'V' without adjusting the operator, leaving the operator invalid.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=', and each side must have at least one numeral or valid expression; do not drop symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After applying a candidate move, before evaluating numeric equality.
matchstick.example: Producing 'VIII - I' which lacks an '=' sign and a left‑hand side.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Use a lookup of common single‑stick numeral changes (e.g., V↔X (+5), I↔V (+4), I↔X (+9)) and their associated value changes; only these transformations are feasible with one stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When matching the numeric discrepancy to a possible numeral change.
matchstick.example: Attempting to change 'IV' (4) to 'II' (2) as if a single stick could do it, which is not in the lookup.

matchstick.title: Maintain exactly one equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from the '=' sign, ensure the remaining symbol stays a valid operator (e.g., turning '=' into '-' is not allowed because the equation would lose its equality).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a candidate move involves the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from '=' and ending up with a single '-' sign, leaving no '=' in the equation.

matchstick.title: Operator sign change impact
matchstick.principle: If a stick move changes an operator (e.g., '+' to '-'), account for the sign reversal in the numeric evaluation of the term; the equation must still balance after the sign change.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After applying a move that alters an operator, recompute the side values with the new sign.
matchstick.example: Turning '+' into '-' without adjusting the right‑hand side, resulting in 15 = 8 - 2, which is false.

matchstick.title: Single‑stick move feasibility
matchstick.principle: When proposing a stick relocation, ensure the move corresponds to a known single‑stick transformation: the source character must be able to lose a stick and remain a valid Roman numeral or operator, and the destination character must be able to gain that stick and become a valid Roman numeral or operator. Discard any candidate that would require more than one stick or produce a shape not in the transformation lookup.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During candidate generation, before accepting a transformation, verify that both source and destination changes are listed in the known single‑stick transformation table.
matchstick.example: Changing IV to II and III to VII (as in 'IX = II + VII') – although the resulting equation is numerically correct, the move would require moving a V (two sticks) and thus is not a single‑stick transformation.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a symbol without checking whether the remaining shape corresponds to any valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick removal, verify that the source character still matches a standard Roman numeral or allowed operator.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on making a syntactically valid equation but does not recompute the side values to ensure they are equal.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑evaluate both sides of the equation after each candidate move and accept only those that balance numerically.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: In the rush to apply a stick move, the model accidentally removes symbols such as the equality sign or an entire term.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that the final string still contains exactly one '=', at least one numeral on each side, and all original operators (except those intentionally changed).

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: When a stick changes an operator (e.g., '+' to '-'), the model forgets that the arithmetic sign of the term flips, breaking the balance.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Whenever an operator is altered, recompute the affected side with the new sign before accepting the move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model proposes transformations that would require moving two or more sticks (e.g., turning a V into a V elsewhere) or adds sticks without a corresponding removal.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce that exactly one stick is removed from a source character and added to a destination character; no sticks may be created or destroyed.
